summary: Add a tenant-scoped MCP client account capability (settings CRUD, one-time bearer token issuance) and wire it as cmd/mcp's first non-deny IdentityResolver, closing the deny-by-default gap left open since Task 018 without inventing a second IAM system or touching the Connector SDK boundary.

impacts.evidence: mcp_client_accounts is a new tenant-scoped table (organization_id/workspace_id, RLS forced); the resolver parses org/workspace/account IDs from the presented bearer token to build a tenancy.Scope before ever querying the table, since Postgres RLS has no scope to enforce before one is known and MCP carries no JWT the way REST does.

Only a SHA-256 token_hash is persisted; the raw bearer token is generated and returned exactly once, at creation, and is never logged or stored again. The create/disable audit summary excludes the token.
Three additive OpenAPI 0.17.0 operations under /settings/mcp-accounts(:disable); no existing operation changed. contracts/sdk/generated-manifest.json and all three SDKs regenerated (115 operations).
No EventBus schema is published or consumed by this capability.

This change is entirely inside the application/settings surface (internal/app/api, internal/app/mcp) and a new platform_capability/infrastructure_adapter pair; it does not touch the Connector SDK, connectors/, or internal/platform/builtinruntime.

Migration 000014_mcp_client_accounts.sql is a normal post-baseline expand migration adding one table; the immutable 000001-000011 pre-v1 squash and 000012-000013 are unchanged. deploy/postgres/catalog.tsv (the file the community deployment migrate.sh entrypoint actually reads) was regenerated to match migrations/catalog.json; scripts/check-community-deployment.sh verifies this drift can't recur silently.

Authentication is a constant-time (crypto/subtle) comparison of the presented secret's SHA-256 hash against the stored token_hash; the token's embedded organization/workspace/account IDs are only a routing hint, never trusted on their own. Verified live: a tampered token and a disabled account's previously-valid token both return 401.

Account create/disable are audited as write_sensitive. settings.mcp_accounts.write (create/disable) is admin-only; settings.mcp_accounts.read extends to manager/operator/viewer, matching the settings.ai_providers.* pattern. This capability does not itself grant tool execution: cmd/mcp's Governor remains unavailableGovernor{}, a pre-existing, separately tracked gap (see ADR 0098) confirmed still open by this task's live verification (tools/list returns an empty array; tools/call is denied).
Every create/disable call is captured with actor, correlation id and a bounded summary (label, permissions) that excludes the token.
This capability performs no remote-state synchronization; there is nothing to reconcile.
No outbound call is made by this capability; it only authenticates inbound MCP callers. No inbound webhook surface is added.
No new SLO/latency-bearing remote dependency is introduced; the resolver performs one indexed Postgres lookup per MCP call.

Disabling an mcp_client_accounts row (soft-disable; DELETE is revoked at the schema level) immediately stops further authentication for that account, verified live; no other component depends on this table.

internal/platform/mcpaccounts and internal/app/mcp/identity_test.go cover token encode/decode round-trip, ValidateCreate rejection paths, and the resolver's accepted/missing-header/tampered-secret/disabled-account/wrong-tenant paths. No Connector SDK conformance suite applies (this task does not touch connectors/); live verification against the running Docker stack with a real Keycloak-issued token is recorded in tasks/issues/126-mcp-client-accounts.md instead.
